title: Mamdani moves to disband NYPD protest-control unit – Politico
content:
The New York mayor is reportedly considering a civilian-led replacement for the police unit, which has faced accusations of excessive force

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist, is finalizing plans to disband a specialized police unit responsible for counterterrorism and crowd control, Politico reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Mamdani pledged to dismantle the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG) during his 2025 mayoral campaign following accusations that its officers used excessive force against protesters.

According to Politico, the mayor is considering replacing the SRG’s protest-response function with a civilian-led unit focused on de-escalation, which could assist police in making arrests when necessary. The new unit could operate under Mamdani’s Office of Community Safety, established earlier this year. The plan could be announced as early as this week and formalized through an executive order.

Read more

“As the mayor has said, our administration will disband the Strategic Response Group and separate protest response from counterterrorism,” Mamdani’s spokeswoman, Dora Pekec, said, promising further details soon.

Established in 2015, the SRG came under increased scrutiny over its handling of the nationwide unrest sparked by the killing of George Floyd by a Minneapolis police officer in 2020. In 2023, the NYPD agreed to restrict the unit’s deployment at peaceful demonstrations and prohibit the practice of surrounding and trapping protesters without grounds for arrest.

New York City Public Advocate Jumaane Williams has called for the SRG to be removed from protest policing, arguing that its aggressive tactics escalated peaceful demonstrations into violent confrontations. He also accused the NYPD of obstructing misconduct investigations.

Mamdani has argued that counterterrorism operations should be separated from policing demonstrations to protect constitutional rights while maintaining public safety. Last month, the mayor ordered the first comprehensive review of the NYPD’s use-of-force policies in a decade, aiming to “strengthen accountability when police officers are accused of serious misconduct.”

Mamdani’s broader police reform agenda has drawn criticism from police unions. In October, Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry accused the mayor of appeasing his “radical base,” warning that the proposed overhaul would not make New Yorkers safer.

Scott Munro, the president of the Detectives Endowment Association, accused Mamdani of seeking to dismantle vital police units rather than support officers, warning that “New Yorkers should be worried.”

title: Israel bars French presidential hopeful over Gaza flotilla pledge
content:
Jean-Luc Melenchon vowed to send French warships to escort pro-Palestinian activists

Israel has banned French left-wing presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon from entering the country after he vowed to deploy warships to escort activist flotillas seeking to break the blockade of Gaza.

The Israeli Foreign Ministry also imposed an entry ban on Mathilde Panot, the parliamentary leader of Melenchon’s La France Insoumise (LFI) party.

“Both have made statements spreading blood libels against Israel, while Jean-Luc Melenchon has also called for French naval vessels to escort illegal flotillas to Gaza,” the ministry said in a statement on Thursday.

“The State of Israel will respond firmly to those who seek to harm it.”

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called the move “a demagogic decision made by a government that has repeatedly violated international law.” He argued that the ban will only help LFI to “thrive on exploiting the Israeli-Palestinian conflict for political gain.”

According to recent opinion polls, Melenchon ranks second behind Marine Le Pen of the right-wing National Rally (RN) in voting intentions for the 2027 presidential election. LFI is one of the largest opposition parties in the French parliament.

Read more

A vocal critic of Israel, Melenchon has pledged to “take direct action” to support Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank if elected president.

“French naval vessels will, if necessary, escort flotillas of citizens mobilized to assert their rights,” he said on Saturday, referring to civilian boats attempting to reach Gaza. Israel has repeatedly intercepted the flotillas at sea and deported foreign activists.

Melenchon said on Thursday that he has never sought to enter Israel and reiterated his accusations of “genocide in Gaza,” as well as his opposition to the expansion of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, and what he described as the gradual annexation of southern Lebanon and the Golan Heights.

The entry bans came shortly after France refused entry to Israeli settlement leader Yossi Dagan, who heads the Samaria Regional Council in the West Bank. The UN considers Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank illegal under international law and a major obstacle to the establishment of an independent Palestinian state.

Israel previously barred foreign politicians, journalists, and activists who are critical of its policies toward Palestinians. In 2019, it denied entry to US Representatives Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib. In 2025, French-Palestinian European Parliament member Rima Hassan, who represents LFI, was also denied entry.

Israel has dismissed accusations of genocide and blamed Hamas for the devastation in Gaza, where more than 74,600 Palestinians have been killed and over 176,000 wounded since October 2023, according to the enclave’s Health Ministry.

title: German democracy satisfaction hits decades-low – study
content:
Two-thirds of Germans are dissatisfied with the political system, particularly in the former East German states

Two in three Germans are dissatisfied with how democracy functions in their country, according to the latest Leipzig Authoritarianism Study conducted by researchers at Leipzig University in cooperation with the Heinrich Boll Foundation and the Otto Brenner Foundation.

The findings, published on Wednesday, show that satisfaction with democracy as experienced in everyday life has fallen to just 33.3%, down from 42.3% in 2024. It is the lowest level recorded since researchers began measuring the indicator in 2006.

Discontent is particularly pronounced in the former East Germany, where only 22.8% of respondents expressed satisfaction, compared with around 36% in the west.

More than half of Germans expressed at least some sympathy for either “nostalgic idealization of the past” or “apocalyptic expectations of the future,” according to the study.

The survey involved 2,507 respondents interviewed from March 16 to June 3.

Read more

The findings follow an INSA poll showing that 82% of Germans are dissatisfied with Chancellor Friedrich Merz and his government. Around 60% said their personal circumstances have worsened since he took office.

Merz became chancellor following snap elections in February 2025, after promising to revive the struggling economy. However, economic difficulties have persisted, while his government has increased military spending, maintained financial and military support for Ukraine, and advocated for reforms to Germany’s welfare system.

The chancellor urged Germans to work more, saying the “welfare state as we have it today can no longer be financed.”

Merz refused to change course after his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) suffered crushing defeats to the anti-immigration, Euroskeptic Alternative for Germany (AfD) in September’s regional elections in the eastern states of Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Merz described the latter result as a “disaster.”

The CDU’s coalition partners, the Social Democrats, have called for a formal review that could pave the way for a ban on the AfD following its sweeping victories in both eastern states. The party denounced the move as an attempt to suppress political opposition and undermine democracy.

title: Denmark ‘moving towards dictatorship’ – MP to RT (VIDEO)
content:
Jacob Harris snubbed Zelensky and accused Copenhagen of prioritizing Ukraine over its own citizens

Denmark is “moving towards a dictatorship,” independent MP Jacob Harris has told RT in an exclusive interview. The Citizen’s Party lawmaker defended his refusal to stand and applaud Vladimir Zelensky during the Ukrainian leader’s controversial address to the Danish parliament.

Harris sat with his arms crossed as other lawmakers gave Zelensky, who openly mocked US President Donald Trump during his speech, a standing ovation on Wednesday. He later posted photos of his protest on X.

His protest was condemned by Danish politicians. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen called it a provocation, while opposition leader Inger Stojberg accused Harris of “doing [Russian President Vladimir] Putin’s bidding.” 

Et diktatur kommer ikke fra den ene dag til den anden. Det vokser frem gennem tavshed, når befolkningen holder op med at sige fra. Demokratiet kræver, at vi tør stille spørgsmål – også når det er ubelejligt for magthaverne. https://t.co/nl8pinTdEG

— Jacob Harris - Folketingsmedlem (@JParti91252) November 11, 2026

Speaking to RT on Thursday, Harris accused the Danish government of undermining democratic rules by allowing a foreign leader to address parliament from its main podium.

“According to our democratic laws, you have to be elected to the Danish parliament before you are allowed to speak there,” he said.

Harris accused Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen of setting aside parliamentary rules for political reasons, calling the decision a move towards dictatorship.

Read more

The Danish parliament has rejected his interpretation, explaining that Zelensky’s address was not a formal parliamentary sitting.

Harris also criticized Copenhagen’s financial support for Kiev, arguing that spending billions on Ukraine while ordinary Danes struggle with rising living costs is “wrong.” 

“People can no longer afford the same standard of living they enjoyed three years ago, and then they see Zelensky come to Denmark and leave with billions,” he told RT.

His remarks came two days after Copenhagen announced another 4.8 billion Danish kroner ($710 million) in military aid for Kiev.

Denmark has committed more than $12.2 billion in military and civilian assistance to Ukraine since 2022, according to its Foreign Ministry. During Zelensky’s visit, Frederiksen reaffirmed Copenhagen’s support, vowing to back Ukraine until the end of the conflict.

Harris met Russian Ambassador to Denmark Vladimir Barbin in Copenhagen on Tuesday, describing their talks as “respectful” and that the two called for a more neutral Danish policy towards the Ukraine conflict. He had also met Ukraine’s ambassador the previous week.

title: Fantasy vs. reality: The confusion of the willing and Ukraine peace talks
content:
‘Europe’ now has a seat at the negotiating table, now the challenge will be to speak with one voice

In their most recent talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner apparently secured a place for ‘Europe’ at the negotiating table with Russia. European leaders will have to overcome deep factional divides and square away their most ideologically-driven fantasists to have any influence over the talks.

“The Europeans will join at the next meeting, which we consider to be a very important moment,” Witkoff told reporters in Moscow on Thursday, before he and Kushner departed for Ireland to brief Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky and his EU backers. 

The Kremlin has not set a date for the next round of talks, nor has Moscow confirmed the precise extent of European participation. However, as Kushner pointed out the previous day, Europe has a more immediate problem on its hands : “If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf,” he said, “that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation.”

The US president’s son-in-law is not the first American to express bewilderment at the absence of a common voice in Europe, and there will likely be much talk around this question now that the invitation has been secured by US President Donald Trump’s diplomatic team. So who is “Europe”? 

Rumsfeld’s “New Europe”

After Danish Foreign Minister Knud Borge Andersen met with US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger on behalf of the nine-member EEC in 1973, Kissinger complained that Andersen seemed to speak for Europe, but lacked any real authority to do so. “We seem to be talking to those who can’t negotiate and those who can negotiate won’t talk to us,” he remarked.

Three decades later, Donald Rumsfeld faced staunch opposition from Belgium, France, and Germany as he attempted to drum up European backing for the illegal invasion of Iraq. However, he received salivating support from Britain, Italy, Poland, and the so-called ‘Vilnius Ten’ – a Baltic and Eastern European bloc with a civil society throbbing with American cash – that enthusiastically signed up to combat “the nexus of terrorism and dictators with weapons of mass destruction.”

The newbies, Rumsfeld figured, were the only Europeans worth talking to. “You’re thinking of ‘Europe’ as Germany and France,” he told a reporter six weeks before the war. “I don’t. I think that’s old Europe. If you look at the entire NATO Europe today, the center of gravity is shifting to the east.”

Who is “Europe” now?

The fault lines identified by Rumsfeld are still visible, and there are three broad camps competing for the position of “voice of Europe.”

The realists

‘Europe’ and ‘foreign policy realism’ rarely appear in the same sentence these days, but among some of “old Europe’s” leaders, there is a realization that the continent will have to acknowledge the limits of its pro-Ukraine stance and take part in talks, before it is overtaken by them.

French President Emmanuel Macron and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni could be considered figureheads, with Macron proposing last December that Europe find an envoy “in the coming weeks.” Meloni declared that the French president “is right on this,” and that “if Europe decides to take part in this phase of negotiations by talking only to one of the two sides, I fear that in the end the positive contribution it can make will be limited.”

Read more

Even German Chancellor Friedrich Merz – despite pivoting his economy into militarization mode and demanding the EU steal billions of Russian sovereign assets – has called on the bloc to “find a balance again with our largest European neighbor.”

Finnish President Alexander Stubb, floated in EU-funded media as a possible envoy to Moscow, along with Meloni, joined Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store to call Putin last month.

“Realism” is a relative term here. All of the aforementioned leaders remain committed to arming Ukraine and pushing for peace on Kiev’s terms, while support for the theft of Russia’s assets remains strong across the EU. Stubb and Store offered “no change in Europe’s approach” to Ukraine during their phone call, according to Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever has also placed himself in the realist camp, arguing that seizing the €210 billion ($236 billion) worth of Russian assets, a move he has blocked, would collapse trust in the European financial system.

The maximalists

The golden children of Rumsfeld’s “new Europe” are full-throttle maximalists. They consider any talks with Russia a betrayal of Ukraine, and remain determined to fight, as Putin has said, “to the last Ukrainian.”

Read more

Their poster boy, Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, reacted with shock when Kushner announced last week that he and Trump were working on an agreement that would “address the security concerns of all sides” in Europe. He told reporters that “the last thing we want is Western Europe dealing with Russia, over the heads of the east Europeans.”

The belief that Ukraine can inflict a military defeat on Russia is a core tenet of European maximalism. Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics made this clear in 2024 when he openly stated “Russia must be destroyed.” Sikorski’s calls for “aggressive” NATO exercises to destabilize Russia’s exclave of Kaliningrad, former Lithuanian Foreign Minister Gabrielius Landsbergis’ demand that NATO leaders remove “all red lines and de-escalation policies” on Russia, and Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal’s likening of Putin to a “rat in a corner” are just three examples of the maximalist rhetoric radiating from Eastern Europe and the Baltics.

Moscow views these “new Europeans” as hysterical, reactionary, and paranoid. Even the US has told them to pipe down, with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby reportedly ordering the Baltic states last month not to “make noise” and stop “poking” Russia.

To the maximalists, even symbolic outreach to Moscow is unconscionable. After Stubb and Store spoke to Putin last month, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen complained that the call had “not been coordinated with the rest of us,” referring to a group reportedly including her and Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, two of the most hardline anti-Russian voices in the EU.

The fantasists

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas wield significantly more power than their predecessors did when Rumsfeld toured Europe in 2003. Von der Leyen has no electorate to answer to, nor has she authority to dictate policy, however she likes to present herself in such a light.  

Read more

The commission still relies on unanimity among the EU’s member states to approve its loans, aid packages, and sanctions, and it has no military power to back up its diktats and proclamations. Brussels and NATO are, however, steadily coalescing in ever closer union.

What the commission has are appeals to fantasy. Von der Leyen has insisted that the EU have veto power over any potential peace deal negotiated between Moscow, Kiev, and Washington, that Ukraine be allowed to keep its pre-conflict borders, and that Moscow be forced to pay reparations to Kiev.

Kallas’ position is even more loosely tethered to reality, with her repeated calls for representation at the negotiating table interspersed with quotes from Marvel superhero movies – “Europeans, assemble!” – and suggestions to dismember Russia into “many smaller nations.”

Von der Leyen’s and Kallas’ hubris has ruled them out as negotiators – both in the eyes of the Kremlin and their fellow Europeans. “How can you discuss anything with Kaja Kallas?” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov remarked to reporters earlier this year. Brussels, he added, is full of “semi-literate, incompetent functionaries.”

A reckoning in Dublin

A compromise in Dublin

European Council President Antonio Costa followed through on his promise to discuss the creation of an envoy during talks at the EU’s summit in Dublin this week. However, the compromise he reached with EU leaders will leave nobody satisfied. Instead of a single envoy, ‘Europe’ will be represented by France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK at the national security adviser level, and by the European Commission and Council at leader-level discussions.

Despite selecting seven separate entities, which include all three European factions – realists, maximalists, and fantasists – Costa insisted that the panel of interlocutors will be able “to speak with one voice.”

Read more

Moscow on maximalists and fantasists

Russia maintains that it is open to serious discussions, but Peskov noted on Wednesday that “for the moment, the statements we hear from the Europeans do not indicate any desire on their part to contribute to progress along a peaceful path.”

“They [top European politicians] are engaged in a group deception of the Ukrainian people. They finance and supply one of the fighting sides with weapons… It contributes to the mass death of the civilian population. And therefore, we do not really understand what we can talk about with them,” Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky told journalists after the Abu Dhabi talks concluded on Wednesday.

title: Progress made in Ukraine peace talks – Russian deputy FM
content:
European involvement could derail diplomatic efforts, Sergey Ryabkov has told RT

The two-day trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the US in Abu Dhabi this week have brought progress toward settling the Ukraine conflict, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov has told RT in an exclusive interview. However, involving European governments in the process could undermine diplomatic efforts, he warned.

Ryabkov was among the Russian delegates at the negotiations, which concluded on Wednesday with an agreement in principle on a major prisoner exchange. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner subsequently traveled to Moscow, where they met Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday for talks lasting around two and a half hours.

Ryabkov noted that the latest round in Abu Dhabi differed from previous meetings, with American representatives seeking to make discussions more concrete. Much of the attention focused on a future European security architecture that could support a lasting settlement and prevent “uncontrolled escalation,” he said.

“We have made progress. That is an indisputable fact,” Ryabkov said, while cautioning that previous diplomatic advances had been followed by setbacks and attempts to derail the process.

“Bringing the Europeans into the negotiating process could mean a reversal and the disruption of efforts,” the diplomat warned.

He pointed to a fundamental divide between European governments and both Moscow and Washington, adding that they rejected Russia’s approach and appeared equally opposed to proposals advanced by the US administration.

Read more

Ryabkov said that European governments had shown “not the slightest desire to exercise common sense” while continuing to recklessly support Kiev. He described the gap between their declared support for a settlement and their actual policies as one rooted in “hypocrisy and lies.”

Those who had previously sought to derail diplomatic efforts should recognize that the situation is changing “not in Kiev’s favor” and draw lessons from past setbacks, the Russian diplomat said.

Western European representatives were not part of the trilateral negotiations, although they held separate consultations with the American and Ukrainian teams. On Wednesday, Vladimir Zelensky demanded that European countries agree on a representative to join the peace process by the end of November.

Moscow has repeatedly questioned Europe’s credibility, citing its continued military and financial support for Kiev and calls for Russia’s strategic defeat. It has also rejected calls for an unconditional ceasefire coming from Brussels, arguing that such a pause would allow Ukrainian forces to regroup and rearm.

Putin also addressed the issue on Thursday, telling Witkoff and Kushner that Russia wanted Washington to work with European governments to establish whether they sought peace or war. He also reiterated Moscow’s opposition to foreign troops in Ukraine, warning that their presence would threaten Russian national security and make them legitimate military targets.

title: Dublin summit: European leaders double down on the Zelensky disaster
content:
With Moscow absent and peace efforts elsewhere advancing, the gathering was just a show of stubborn loyalty to a failing proxy war

Let’s start with the obvious, which, oddly enough, remains largely unnoticed: If the summit of the European Political Community (EPC), a formally informal gathering that brings together the high and mighty of NATO-EU Europe plus friends, was serious about reflecting Europe, then Russia (and, by the way, Belarus, too) would have been invited.

The fact that Moscow is not present is, once you think about it, a striking anomaly, even if Western mainstream media framing has been quite effective at making the obviously strange appear to be the new normal.

Russia’s longstanding exclusion is, of course, also very telling. At the risk of re-stating the obvious, it reflects NATO-EU Europe’s fundamentally flawed, catastrophically costly (including for Ukraine), and very obstinate policy of waging a proxy war against Russia, while using up Ukraine and Ukrainians.

It’s a shame: Europe could have been the ideal framework for preventing, or at least quickly ending, the Ukraine War by offering honest mediation, facilitating real compromise, and, last but not least, helping review and revise a continental security structure destabilized and, in effect, ruined by a reckless NATO expansion based on brazen Western cheating.

Yet, unsurprisingly, NATO-EU Europe has always done the opposite: from being too arrogant to listen to Russian President Vladimir Putin’s clear warning in Munich in 2007, through the foul compromise of the Bucharest summit one year later and the perfectly misguided EU Association Agreement designed to force Kiev to make an impossible choice between the EU and Russia, to taking over from Washington as the main proxy war promoter and key obstacle to peace – NATO-EU Europe has a consistent record of making things go awfully wrong and then making them worse and worse again.

Read more

In that sense, the great Dublin let’s-all-hate-on-Russia-some-more fest is simply very boring. But there are aspects to it that – notwithstanding its makers’ and participants’ worst intentions – merit attention.

Take, for instance, French President Emmanuel Macron’s open announcement that the US has left its European vassals (not Macron’s words, of course, but let’s make him a little more honest) holding the Ukraine War bag all on their own. Strictly speaking, Macron, as is so often the case, is not factually correct: Zelensky’s recurring complaints about Starlink/Starshield slowdowns are only possible because these massive US resources, for instance, are still – wrongly – made available to his regime, hellbent as it is on escalating open warfare far beyond Ukraine.

If only Washington had really fully retreated from the proxy war! Perhaps the war would be over already, and many Ukrainians and Russians would still be alive.

Yet Macron’s slightly hysterical misreading of US behavior does betray something very real, namely an acute and deep sense of abandonment among Washington’s vassals. One day, probably far in the future, some of them may even begin to draw the correct conclusions from it.

But today is not that day. Instead, it seems that the Dublin summit’s main message regarding its proxy war and the authoritarian, man-hunting, ultra-corrupt Zelensky regime deployed to manage it on the ground is “stay the course.”

Halfway self-respecting proxy war sponsors would long have refused to touch Zelensky with a bargepole – “here’s the money but we really can’t be seen with you” – due to his regime’s outrageous and essentially open embezzlement of their funds (they do not care about his massive brutalization of ordinary Ukrainians, it goes without saying). Not a week goes by without another “Mindich,” “Carthage,” “Khimprom,” or “Sokolov” mega-scandal.

Read more

And yet, the opposite is happening. In Dublin, too, the boss of bosses of the rapacious and quite murderous crime syndicate that the Zelensky regime really is gets the VIP treatment. And, of course, also license to lecture anyone in sight on what they must do and owe “Ukraine,” that is, him and his cronies. Nothing has changed.

What may be even worse, Zelensky is also permitted – or, most likely, encouraged, for instance by his most submissive fan, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz – to publicly gripe at a recent key shift in serious diplomacy about ending the Ukraine War: alert to dangers to his income streams, power, and political survival, Ukraine’s de facto dictator has used Dublin to complain about, in essence, Washington’s apparent willingness to finally take seriously Russia’s demand for a comprehensive review of security structures. And yet without that, peace won’t come.

Zelensky’s unshaken – at least in public – permission to play dissatisfied-consumer-from-hell and berate his sponsors is even more remarkable as the Dublin summit is being held against an international context with which it clashes profoundly. Consider a few places and what they stand for regarding the Ukraine War: Abu Dhabi, Moscow, and, soon probably, Shenzhen. Different as the specific formats are or will be, what they all have in common is that real if not yet successful work is done or likely to be done there to bring peace about.

And yet, quite like their creature Zelensky, the NATO-EU establishments resist precisely that outcome. It is true that we are seeing signs of – auspicious – disunity. Norway and Finland, for instance, have emitted weak but intriguing signals of rediscovering a sense of reality.

Yet, overall and as of now, Dublin shows us another, still dominant side of NATO-EU Europe: too weak and too submissive to Washington to be a power on its own in the emerging multipolar order, but hellbent to use all its resources to be a spoiler. It is sad to have to say this as a genuine European, but NATO-EU Europe is a caricature of our common identity. If there’s hope, it lies in its weakness.

title: US no longer needs Iran deal – Trump
content:
The president has redirected J.D. Vance toward domestic issues after the vice president blamed the conflict for Republicans’ midterm defeat

Washington no longer needs a deal with Iran, US President Donald Trump has declared. He has directed Vice President J.D. Vance to focus instead on alleged corruption and crime in Democrat-run states and cities.

The announcement follows Vance’s criticism of the US-Israeli war on Iran, which he blamed for Republicans’ defeat in last week’s midterm elections. On Wednesday, the vice president questioned whether the conflict had been worth its cost. Vance had previously pursued diplomatic efforts to end the war and reportedly favored reaching an agreement with Tehran over continued military pressure.

In a Truth Social post on Thursday, Trump ordered Vance to devote his “complete and total attention” to tackling the domestic issue, arguing that a sweeping corruption crackdown could help balance the federal budget.

“We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,” Trump wrote. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”

Read more

Trump offered no explanation for his claim about Iranian money, which some media outlets have interpreted as a reference to frozen Iranian assets. Tehran estimates the funds at more than $100 billion, largely consisting of oil and gas revenues held in foreign banks under US sanctions.

His assertion of control over the Strait of Hormuz appears to refer to the US naval blockade, which restricts shipping to and from Iranian ports while allowing vessels serving other Gulf countries to pass.

On Monday, Trump said he would hold off on further strikes against Iran after Gulf states urged Washington to avoid another escalation.

Iran, however, has also asserted its authority over the strategic waterway.

Iran’s parliament speaker and chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, told Al Jazeera on Wednesday that Tehran had reached an understanding with Oman on managing the strait as part of its seven-point peace proposal.

Read more

Ghalibaf insisted that Hormuz would “never return” to its pre-war status, when foreign vessels could transit without Iranian permission. Tehran is now seeking greater control over shipping through the vital oil trade route.

The Iranian official said Tehran had submitted its peace terms through Qatari mediators but had yet to receive a formal response from Washington.

The proposal calls for lifting US sanctions and the naval blockade, releasing frozen Iranian assets and ending hostilities across the region.

“The ball is now in the American court,” Ghalibaf said.

title: Trump floats Tim Cook as Nvidia chief after ‘Chinese honeypot’ scandal
content:
The US president has suggested the former Apple CEO as a successor to Jensen Huang, who resigned following reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for Beijing

US President Donald Trump has suggested that former Apple CEO Tim Cook take over Nvidia following the resignation of its longtime chief Jensen Huang, who stepped down after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China

“A legend replaces a legend!” Trump wrote, floating Cook, who now chairs Apple’s board, as a potential successor to Huang. The American president had previously defended Huang as “an amazing guy,” saying he believed that the executive had been unaware of the alleged espionage.

Trump and Cook have maintained ties for years, with the president previously claiming that the Apple executive had called him to “kiss my ass” while seeking help during his first term. In August 2025, Cook visited Trump in the Oval Office, presenting him with a plaque featuring a 24-karat gold base as Apple announced plans to increase its US investment commitment to $600 billion over four years. Trump later praised Cook as an “incredible guy,” describing their relationship as “long and very nice.”

Nvidia announced on Thursday that Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive, and board member “effective immediately,” ending his 33-year tenure. Finance chief Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia seeks a permanent replacement.

The crisis erupted over reports linking Huang to Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a businesswoman formerly associated with Singapore-based Nvidia chip buyer Megaspeed International. The New York Times and Financial Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected her of gathering information for Beijing and influencing Huang to seek looser chip export restrictions.

Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun calling the Chinese spy narrative “a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear.”

Read more

Huang admitted on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without identifying the woman. 

On Wednesday, the New York Times wrote that Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him. 

Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation into the affair on November 8. It initially backed Huang and said it had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised. 

The subsequent resignation announcement gave no specific reason or explanation for his departure.

Nvidia and Huang also face a proposed shareholder class action alleging that they deliberately concealed the relationship and misled investors about the risks.

Following the announcement, Nvidia shares plunged more than 13% in early trading on Thursday, wiping over $575 billion off its market value and leaving the stock down roughly 17% over the past year. On Wednesday, its valuation had already fallen below $4 trillion for the first time in over a year.

READ MORE: Trump backs ‘honeypot-hit’ Nvidia boss

The turmoil has spread across the AI sector and weighed on the broader US market, erasing hundreds of billions of dollars in share value. Nvidia-linked cloud computing provider CoreWeave fell about 11% at the opening, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also declined.

Polymarket traders, meanwhile, were pricing a roughly 12% chance of an “AI bubble burst” by year-end.

title: WAN-IFRA stands with AMI Colombia as threats against the press escalate
content:
According to our member association AMI, security alerts led to the evacuation of Caracol Televisión, Caracol Radio, RCN and Semana in Bogotá. AMI also reports continuing threats and acts of violence against journalists in different regions of Colombia, and public statements targeting media outlets and reporters. As AMI points out, these are separate events, but they raise a common question: what place does Colombia give its press?

AMI notes that public stigmatisation of journalism and violence against it, particularly in the regions, have reached alarming levels in recent years, and that the IAPA’s Chapultepec Index places Colombia among the countries where press freedom indicators have deteriorated the most. AMI’s figures show that more than 2,000 attacks were recorded against hundreds of journalists between August 2022 and July 2026, including ten murders, four of them in 2026. On average, according to AMI, a journalist is threatened every two days.

Press freedom and the right to information are not privileges of the people who report the news. They are guarantees that belong to citizens, who need a diversity of voices to understand what is happening and form their own opinions. When threats against journalists and media outlets create a climate of intimidation that leads to censorship and self-censorship, society as a whole has the most to lose.

WAN-IFRA joins AMI in calling on the Colombian authorities to:

  • adopt concrete public policies that protect the practice of journalism, with protection mechanisms and guarantees that outlast any single government;
  • reconsider the language they use about media outlets and journalists. The words of people in positions of authority carry more weight than those of any other public actor. They can build a climate of respect for those who inform society, or one of contempt.

Pluralism cannot be imposed by decree. It grows when criticism is accepted as a normal part of democracy and a diversity of voices is understood to strengthen both those who govern and those who are governed. A society that respects differing opinions, promotes media pluralism and guarantees the free exercise of journalism is a safer society.

title: Growing Movement Boycotts Krill Products as CCAMLR Fails to Protect Antarctic Ecosystems
content:
A seal navigates the icy waters of the Antarctic—an ecosystem under mounting pressure from commercial fishing and climate change. Credit: Our Antarctica/Shawn Heinrichs

By Oritro Karim
UNITED NATIONS, Nov 12 2026 (IPS)

On October 30, the 45th annual meeting of the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR-45) concluded in Hobart, Australia. After another year of negotiations without a consensus reached on Antarctic marine protection measures or krill fishing regulations, conservation groups are urging consumers and retailers to boycott all krill products.

Widely regarded as a vital, shared global commons, the Antarctic is home to trillions of krill. A keystone species, krill from the Southern Ocean form the backbone of the polar ecosystem, sustaining nearly every major predator, from seabirds and seals to whales. Antarctic krill possess one of the largest biomasses of any wild animal on Earth, measuring between 379 and 500 million tonnes.

In an exclusive interview with IPS, marine biologist, policy expert, and Antarctic Wildlife Alliance Executive Director Ally Kristan explained that Antarctic krill act as a “tremendous” carbon sink and are critically important for the health of the Southern Ocean. She stressed that the stability of Antarctic marine ecosystems is a major climate driver for the entire globe.

“If you lose krill, you lose the foundation of the entire Southern Ocean food web. So then, all of the predators who feed on krill and the predators who feed on the predators who feed on krill would all be decimated,” said Kristan. “So we do need a healthy Southern Ocean ecosystem, biologically and chemically, to have a healthy climate and to have as much carbon absorbed into these nutrient-rich cold waters of the Southern Ocean.”

Despite their ecological importance, industrial fishing fleets harvest hundreds of thousands of tonnes of krill annually. Given the abundance of krill biomass in the Southern Ocean, Kristan noted that the species is “probably” not being overfished, but the central issue lies with how they are being fished.

She explained that industrial krill fishing is often heavily concentrated in small areas, which can have devastating localized impacts on regional marine fauna. With krill fishing often overlapping with wildlife feeding grounds, polar predators have been increasingly forced to compete with commercial supertrawlers for food.

“Science shows us that the krill fishery and the recovering whale population both probably can’t be supported by krill populations, especially as the climate continues to change,” she said. “Fisheries have a huge compounding impact on all the climate pressures whales are already facing.”

IPS also spoke with Max Bello, an international ocean policy expert and Blue Marine Foundation’s Global MPA Specialist. He underscored the ethical concerns surrounding Antarctic krill extraction, noting that it supplies high-end consumer products, such as omega-3 supplements, pet food, and farmed fish feed, even though viable alternatives exist.

Kristan added that krill fishing has no direct use for addressing human food security. Instead, fleets from wealthy nations in the Global North—primarily Norway and China—exploit this shared global resource to supply high-end markets, risking potentially dire environmental consequences.

She highlighted the commercial market for the luxury Antarctic toothfish—commonly sold under the market name of “Chilean Seabass”—as a key example. Bello echoed these concerns, emphasizing that up to 70 percent of harvested krill goes toward salmon aquaculture, a market “which has proven to be extremely destructive around the entire world, highly polluted.”

Bello stressed that unsustainable krill fishing practices coupled with the Antarctic’s position as an Area Beyond National Jurisdiction (ABNJ) set an alarming precedent, with global powers relying on a shared resource to enrich themselves.

“This definitely creates a big question about our governance of the oceans around the world, where we keep seeing wealthy nations and companies that have the technology and resources to exploit an area that belongs to us all,” said Bello. “So that sends a really worrisome message. A message to our nations that we are basically spectators or witnesses of how other countries continue to build wealth out of the destruction of a common resource.”

He added that the exploitation of Antarctic marine ecosystems has ripple effects that go “beyond money” that we all depend on, such as oxygen, biodiversity, and the “stability of our very vulnerable ecosystem.”

Seventeen years after CCAMLR members pledged to implement a comprehensive network of MPAs, only two have been established. In 2024, CCAMLR allowed the expiration of a critical safeguard designed to spread krill catches across four distinct management zones, which has elicited significant pushback from conservation and environmental justice groups.

Ahead of the summit, conservation groups called on governments to implement four marine protection measures: reinstating restrictions separating industrial fishing areas from wildlife feeding grounds, adopting the Antarctic Peninsula Marine Protected Area (MPA), setting a firm roadmap for completing a network of Southern Ocean MPAs, and introducing caps on krill catch limits. None of these calls were answered.

As CCAMLR continues to fail to deliver meaningful action, a growing global initiative has formed to protect Antarctic marine ecosystems by directly challenging consumer support in the markets. During NYC Climate Week in September, oceanographer Dr. Sylvia Earle and the Antarctic Avengers—a coalition of ocean leaders, policymakers, scientists, and public figures—launched a global boycott of Antarctic krill, urging consumers and retailers alike to reject all krill-derived products.

Several major retailers in the Global North have shown support for this growing movement. In April, Holland & Barrett—one of the United Kingdom’s leading international health and wellness retailers—entirely withdrew from the krill market, ceasing the sale and production of all krill-derived products.

Approximately 94 percent of German drugstores have also announced commitments to cease selling krill products. Two of Australia’s largest supermarket chains—Coles and Woolworths—followed suit. The Antarctic Wildlife Alliance continues to call on American retailers to take similar action.

IPS UN Bureau Report

title: EU member jails woman over pro-Russia TikTok posts
content:
A Latvian court imposed a three-year prison sentence over alleged glorification of war crimes in Ukraine

A court in Riga, Latvia has sentenced a woman to three years in prison over TikTok posts deemed to glorify alleged war crimes committed by Russian forces in Ukraine, LETA news agency reported on Wednesday.

The case is the latest in a series of prosecutions in Latvia over statements deemed supportive of Moscow or critical of Kiev. Since the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022, the Baltic state has tightened restrictions on Russian-language media, cultural activities, and public expressions of pro-Russian sentiment.

According to LETA, the case involved around 20 videos and comments posted by Latvian citizen Tatyana Masenko from April to July 2024. The agency cited several examples of content that prosecutors considered criminal.

One video reportedly showed a Ukrainian serviceman with a prosthetic limb standing in front of a cemetery lined with Ukrainian flags. Masenko captioned it: “Forward, to the gay-European future.”

Another video included a similar message: “Soon, all of you from across gay Europe will be gathered together and sent to defend Ukraine with bags of sunflower seeds and packets.”

Read more

Masenko’s defense argued that the three-year sentence is excessively harsh, noting that she had already spent four months in custody. Her lawyer said the verdict would be appealed.

This comes after a series of similar cases in Latvia. In January, a court sentenced 72-year-old professor Aleksandr Gaponenko to ten years in prison over his participation in an academic roundtable, where he gave a ten-minute speech on discrimination against Russian speakers in Latvia.

The Baltic state, which has a substantial Russian-speaking population, has restricted Russian-language education, removed Soviet-era monuments, and tightened the rules governing the public use of Russian symbols.

Russia has accused Latvia and its Baltic neighbors, Estonia and Lithuania, of pursuing a policy of “extreme Russophobia” and systematically discriminating against Russian-speaking residents under the pretext of national security.

Moscow downgraded diplomatic relations with all three Baltic states in 2023, citing their hostile policies.

Putin-US envoy talks conclude: Latest reactions (Updates, VIDEOS)
content:
The Kremlin has described the meeting as constructive and said Moscow and Washington had agreed to continue diplomatic efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict

Russian President Vladimir Putin has concluded talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow. The Kremlin described the meeting as constructive and confirmed that diplomatic efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict will continue. 

The talks followed two days of US-mediated negotiations between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, which focused on a potential settlement of the conflict and the future European security architecture. 

Senior officials, including Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, and Witkoff, have been speaking to reporters following the meeting. 

RT brings you the key statements and latest developments.

“Constructive” talks

Putin’s negotiations with the US envoys were “substantive, constructive, frank and useful,” Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov told reporters following the meeting.

He said the discussions followed a similar pattern to previous exchanges between the Russian president and American negotiators. 

Read more

Kushner also described the talks with Putin as “very fulsome and detailed,” saying they covered all major issues and would help shape the next round of multilateral negotiations and upcoming discussions with Zelensky.

“Very productive time,” he said.

Witkoff hails progress in peace efforts 

The US special envoy welcomed the resumption of trilateral negotiations between Russia, Ukraine, and the US, pointing to plans for another round of talks. 

“I think progress was made today, yes,” Witkoff told reporters before departing Moscow following his meeting with Putin. 

He noted that few had expected the trilateral format to resume in Abu Dhabi, but the negotiations did restart and another meeting has already been scheduled. “This is what President Trump wants to see,” he added.

Key positions on European security 

Putin reaffirmed Moscow’s proposals for a new European security architecture, including an end to NATO expansion, restrictions on the deployment of weapons systems threatening Russia near its borders, and a return to the military bloc’s force configuration at the time of the 1997 Russia-NATO Founding Act, Ushakov said. 

Moscow considers the existing European security system ineffective and is ready to begin talks with Washington on a new long-term arrangement, which it hopes European countries will also support, he added. 

Read more

European governments have been seeking to join the negotiations but should decide whether they want peace or a continuation of the conflict, according to the Kremlin aide, who said that their actions so far suggest the latter. 

Foreign troops in Ukraine would mean ‘endless war’  

Plans by the European “coalition of the willing” to deploy foreign troops in Ukraine after the conflict would risk prolonging the fighting indefinitely, Ushakov said. 

“This is a recipe for an endless war,” he said. 

Zelensky unwilling to end conflict

Putin and the US envoys also discussed Vladimir Zelensky’s recent remarks about President Donald Trump. 

According to Ushakov, Kiev is reluctant to end the conflict because a settlement would require new elections, potentially threatening Zelensky’s hold on power. 

Major prisoner exchange 

Moscow and Washington backed a proposal discussed during the Abu Dhabi negotiations for what could become a major prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine.

The terms are still being negotiated, Ushakov said, expressing hope that Kiev would honor the agreement reached in principle.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that further work was needed to finalize the exchange, with the Russian Defense Ministry expected to provide details. 

Russia and Ukraine have conducted 35 prisoner exchanges since 2025, involving approximately 5,000 people from each side, according to Ushakov.

Witkoff also commented on the planned prisoner exchange, telling reporters it would be completed “in short order” and describing it as the “largest in history.”

He added that European representatives would join the next round of negotiations, calling their participation “a very big deal.”  

Putin-Trump talks in China

The Russian president and his US counterpart are expected to discuss the Ukraine settlement during the upcoming APEC summit in Shenzhen, according to Ushakov.

Read more

He said that Trump was personally involved in efforts to reach a lasting resolution to the conflict. 

Both Moscow and Washington view the planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping as an important step, Ushakov said. Preparations are underway, with Moscow hoping the first meeting in this format will have a positive impact on international relations. 

Europe’s actions contradict its calls for peace  

European countries are pursuing policies that could prolong the Ukraine conflict despite their stated desire for peace, Peskov said. “They are moving towards continuing the war, expanding the war, but talking about peace.”  

European leaders have yet to agree on who should represent them in negotiations, Peskov added, noting that those seeking direct contact with Moscow risked being ostracized by their counterparts. 

What’s next? 

Witkoff and Kushner are expected to meet Ukrainian and European representatives in Dublin following their talks in Moscow. 

The Kremlin hopes the American negotiators will fully convey Moscow’s position to their Ukrainian and European counterparts, Ushakov said.

title: Pope Leo returns to beloved former home of Chiclayo, Peru
content:
Pope Leo XIV seems omnipresent in Chiclayo. His image is painted in colorful murals, emblazoned on baseball hats and bobbleheads, and celebrated with signs across this city in northern Peru that read: "Welcome home."

Lima is the culinary epicenter of South America. Cusco is the historic capital of the Inca empire and the gateway to Machu Picchu. But Chiclayo has a special claim as home to the Peruvian American pope, who returns there on Friday.

The first U.S.-born pontiff, Leo spent about two decades in Peru as a missionary and church leader, obtaining Peruvian citizenship shortly before he served as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023. He remains beloved here for championing social justice issues and for his closeness to the people, especially the poor.

Many remember how the bishop then known as Robert Prevost led the life-saving purchase of oxygen production plants during the COVID-19 pandemic; how he waded through mud after torrential rains to bring help to the needy; how he celebrated Mass at the local prison. Others recall how he'd drive his pickup truck to remote villages to hand out blankets and sing Christmas songs, and his love of regional dishes like duck with rice and goat stew.

The love is reciprocal

In his first words as the leader of 1.4 billion Catholics, Pope Leo gave a special shoutout in Spanish to his "beloved Diocese of Chiclayo" from the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica. His return reaffirms his affection for Chiclayo's churches, schools and sanctuaries and is widely viewed as the emotional highlight of his South American trip.

"People aren't saying: 'The pope is Peruvian.' They're saying, 'The pope is Chiclayano!'" said the Rev. Jasson Sempertegui, who was his secretary when he led the diocese. "In Chiclayo we like to say: 'The pope is returning home.'"

IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Pope Leo XIV casts mail-in ballot, becoming first pope to vote in US election

It is, Sempertegui said, the most important moment in Chiclayo's history since it was settled in the 16th century by Spanish Franciscan priests as an Indigenous village about 13 kilometers (8 miles) from the Pacific Ocean.

Chiclayo and its people, he said, might have been more influential to the pope than his native Chicago and the Vatican.

The torrent of crises he confronted in Chiclayo including the COVID pandemic, assisting newly arrived Venezuelan migrants, and the devastating floods helped form his pastoral identity.

"He's Chiclayano because he faced the biggest challenges of his pastoral life here," Sempertegui said. "This helped him to connect with people's pain."

From Chicago to Chiclayo

During his time in the city, Leo often repeated a joke: "Chicago, Chiclayo, what difference is there? Only one letter."

A city of about 700,000 people, Chiclayo is the commercial hub of Peru's northern Pacific coast, with highways linking it to the Andes and the Amazon region. Chiclayanos take pride in the city's nickname, "Capital of Friendship," and its proximity to major archeological sites.

"Before, we were an unnoticed, low-profile city," said Zuly Castillo, who worked for Leo when he was bishop. Across from her office, a life-size cardboard cutout of the pope now welcomes visitors to his former residence. "Now we see that he has given us so much and we have become known worldwide."

In Chiclayo, the pope would wake before dawn to pray, then walk to the cathedral in the city center. He listened to confession and was moved by stories of adversity in a city where 20% of residents live in poverty.

He became known as an efficient problem solver, even fixing diocesan cars with YouTube tutorials. He learned local jargon and humor, and sometimes invited priests to join him for a lunch of his lomo saltado (Peru's classic beef and tomato stir-fry) or ceviche (raw fish marinated in lime juice).

A pope who binge-watched 'Prison Break'

In the breaks between prayers, theology classes and chores, the aspiring priests at the city's seminary of Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo remembered how Leo would visit them offering encouragement, sharing a meal, playing tennis.

The Rev. Marcos Ballena, a seminary leader, recalled the glee of seminarians watching TV in the common room when Cardinal Prevost was elected pope. "Everyone jumped as if they had won a World Cup!"

IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Milei's Argentina

Seminarian Jose Miguel Teran agreed: "There are some funny videos where we're all euphoric ... and even more when he said, 'My beloved diocese of Chiclayo', we understood very clearly that this is his home, and we feel him as part of our family."

Darwin Sanchez first met Leo while serving as an altar boy. Soon, he'll have the honor to carry the miter that Leo will wear when celebrating Masses.

"In our youth ministries, with the altar boys there's a surging interest in the vocation because the pope is deemed to be Chiclayano," Sanchez said.

On his breaks in Chiclayo, he liked to watch his beloved Chicago White Sox' baseball games and binge-watch American TV series, like "24" and "Prison Break."

In the working-class neighborhood of San Antonio, people remember him sharing a meal with the needy at a soup kitchen that he inaugurated.

"He told immigrants at the time that we welcomed vulnerable people," said Daria Chavarry, a volunteer at a soup kitchen that has been renamed "Papa Leon XIV."

After a meal near a large poster of the pope, 78-year-old Maria Teresa Santa Cruz said she paid 25 soles (about $3) in three installments to buy a T-shirt of Leo.

"I bought it because we have one more representative here on Earth," she said about Leo's mission to protect the dignity of the poor.

A pope who waded through mud in rubber boots

Leo helped deliver donations in 2017 when hundreds lost their homes as rivers overflooded. He also welcomed Venezuelan migrants escaping their country's political and economic crises and oversaw construction of a temporary shelter and 13 homes.

"This is the place that he gave us for us to build a home again," said Betania Marina Rodriguez, who worked closely with Leo on projects and lives in one of the homes.

She recalled how Leo delivered live chickens to her home during the COVID pandemic, to share with other migrants.

"In him we saw the feeling of hope," Rodriguez said. "He always said that human dignity has no borders."

Rocio Zea lost her home to flooding in 2023 and remembers fondly how Leo took off his priestly robes and waded through the mud in rubber boots to reach the needy.

"He was the first person who came with help and cared about us when everything was flooded and the water reached our necks," said Zea. "It's surreal to think that the person who's been there for you is now the pope the most important person on Earth after God."

He grew so fond of Chiclayo that he hoped to stay put "and even to be buried alongside the diocese's other bishops," Daniel Burke and Scott Detrow write in their book, "American Pope."

But then Pope Francis asked him to return to Rome for an important Vatican job. He teared up in his final Mass with his parishioners.

Prisoners at Chiclayo penitentiary gathered at the carpentry workshop to carve a papal staff before his visit their gift to the missionary who visited them to celebrate Mass and who became the pope.

"There's so much joy over his visit," said the Rev. Elmer Uchofen, the prison chaplain. "We knew he'd come back; Chiclayo is in his heart."

title: Pope Leo returns to beloved former home of Chiclayo, Peru
content:
Pope Leo XIV seems omnipresent in Chiclayo. His image is painted in colorful murals, emblazoned on baseball hats and bobbleheads, and celebrated with signs across this city in northern Peru that read: "Welcome home."

Lima is the culinary epicenter of South America. Cusco is the historic capital of the Inca empire and the gateway to Machu Picchu. But Chiclayo has a special claim as home to the Peruvian American pope, who returns there on Friday.

title: Canada ignores court ruling to bar Russian hockey team
content:
Ottawa says it will not admit Russian players to the upcoming World Junior Championship, even with valid visas

Canada will bar Russian hockey players and officials from the upcoming World Junior Championship, even those with valid visas, the government has announced.

Canadian Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden sought to justify the ban, announced on Wednesday and defying a sports court ruling, by portraying Russian athletes’ participation as a vehicle for “state representation, political legitimacy and propaganda,” adding that immigration authorities will block their entry.
 
“Canada’s position is unequivocal: As long as Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual,” he declared, echoing Prime Minister Mark Carney, who had ruled out Russian participation last week. The tournament runs from December 26 to January 5.
  
Ottawa’s move puts it at odds with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which last month overturned the International Ice Hockey Federation’s (IIHF) suspension of Russia over the Ukraine conflict and ordered its reinstatement for five championships in 2027, including the World Juniors in Canada and the men’s World Championship in Germany. The IIHF expressed disappointment but pledged to comply.

Read more

The ruling sparked boycott threats from several of Kiev's European backers, including Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Latvia, and the Czech Republic, while Germany has called for a fresh IIHF suspension of Russia.

Moscow has accused the boycotters of putting politics above sport. Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev earlier warned that federations defying the CAS ruling could face lawsuits, lose hosting rights or suffer automatic 5-0 defeats under IIHF rules for refusing to play Russia.
 
The Russian Ice Hockey Federation has demanded that the IIHF either guarantee Russia’s participation in Canada or move the tournament elsewhere, according to Match TV.

READ MORE: Russia’s hockey comeback a ‘return to normality’ – German opposition 


Two-time Olympic hockey champion Boris Mikhailov has blasted Ottawa’s decision as politically motivated, joking that Carney might be jealous of Russian NHL star Alexander Ovechkin for smashing Canadian legend Wayne Gretzky’s long-standing record of 894 regular-season goals in April 2025.

Ovechkin himself argued that fans should get to see the world’s best players compete.

Read more

”I’m pretty sure if you ask the fans, the fans want to see the best players out there,” the Washington Capitals captain told reporters Tuesday. “The fans want to see young generation players who are going to be future stars, future NHLers. But you know it’s not up to us.”

Russia remains an ice hockey powerhouse and a member of the sport’s elite 'Big Six'. Soviet and Russian teams have claimed a record 27 World Championship titles and nine Olympic golds, with the legendary Soviet “Red Machine” dominating the sport for decades. The country also remains a major source of hockey talent, producing stars including Ovechkin, Nikita Kucherov, and Andrei Vasilevskiy.

title: One dead, four wounded after shooting near White House (VIDEOS)
content:
The incident occurred in Washington, DC’s Logan Circle neighborhood, about a mile north of the presidential residence

At least one person has been killed and four wounded by a gunman in Washington, DC, interim Metropolitan Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said at a press conference. The shooting occurred about a 15-minute walk from the White House.

Police said the suspect shot one person with a handgun inside a gym before returning to his apartment and shooting four others with a rifle from his balcony.

“Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out,” a witness, who was at a gym when the shooting began, told AP. “One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck.”

Videos and images circulating on social media purport to show heavily armed police stationed on rooftops around an apartment building. Other footage shows officers armed with ballistic shields closing in on what appears to be the same building.

Videos also show a heavy police presence on DC streets after the incident.

Huge police presence in Washington DC for an active shooter. Residents being warned to shelter in place. Am watching SWAT teams get ready to storm a building. 15th St NW at junction with P street. https://t.co/MEuFtcQdUR

— Richard Gaisford (@richardgaisford) November 12, 2026

The suspect, who was found with a self-inflicted gunshot wound and received medical assistance, has since died of his injuries, according to the police chief.

Read more

Of the four people injured in the shooting, one is in critical condition and the other three have non-life-threatening injuries, DC Fire and EMS Chief John Donnelly said at a press conference.

Police identified the suspect as 55-year-old Matt Lambert. “We do know there was a conflict between him and the homeowners association of that building. But at this point, we’re continuing to look into that,” Carroll told reporters.

On his personal website, Lambert described himself as “a seasoned clinician, consultant, and entrepreneur.” He also identified himself as the founder and CEO of MLEM, a healthcare and technology consultancy.

title: EU incapable of speaking with one voice on Ukraine – analyst to RT (VIDEO)
content:
Divisions between major powers have left the bloc without a credible representative for talks with Moscow, Xavier Moreau says

The European Union lacks a diplomatic heavyweight capable of negotiating with Russia, while disagreements between its largest member states have undermined its ability to speak with one voice on Ukraine, Stratpol director Xavier Moreau has told RT.

His comments follow two days of trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US in Abu Dhabi, which concluded on Wednesday, marking the first formal three-way meeting since February. European representatives were excluded from the negotiations, although they held separate discussions with US and Ukrainian officials on Tuesday. Moscow has questioned Europe’s potential contribution to the peace process, accusing EU governments of undermining previous agreements and prolonging the conflict through continued weapons supplies.

“The European Union makes the big European countries weak,” Moreau said, arguing that the bloc’s diplomatic structure has left its most influential members unable to take the lead in potential negotiations with Moscow.

Read more

He questioned who could credibly represent the EU in talks with Russia, dismissing the bloc’s foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, as an unsuitable candidate.

“She’s not very known as a clever diplomat, so the Russians will never accept,” Moreau said, suggesting that any European representative should instead come from Germany, France, or Italy.

However, he argued that the EU’s overlapping national and supranational diplomatic structures have created confusion over who actually speaks for Europe.

“Who is in charge of the diplomacy in the European Union? Brussels, Paris, Germany, or Italy?” he asked.

Moreau also pointed to sharply differing positions among the bloc’s three largest economies. According to the analyst, France has exhausted its financial capacity to support Ukraine, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz remains committed to continued assistance despite mounting difficulties.

Italy, meanwhile, is seeking to distance itself from the conflict, he claimed, while ultimately following Washington’s lead.

Moreau also cited disagreements between Germany and Eastern European countries, including Bulgaria, Czechia, and Romania, which he said are increasingly unwilling to fund Ukraine.

“So a common voice in Europe, it’s not possible,” he concluded.

title: White House warns Democrats over Trump probes
content:
The exchange of threats comes after House Democrats vowed to investigate alleged corruption during Trump’s second term

The White House’s top lawyer has warned the House Democrats that their plans to investigate the administration of US President Donald Trump “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

The dispute follows a pledge by the Democrats to launch a broad series of investigations into the Trump administration after winning control of the House of Representatives in last week’s midterm elections. The probes are expected to focus on alleged corruption, conflicts of interest, and abuses of power.

In a three-page letter issued on Wednesday to incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia, White House counsel Will Scharf argued that congressional investigations must remain within constitutional limits, adding that Garcia and members of the new Congress have “evinced a clear intent to transgress” them. The letter accuses Democrats of “abusive and capricious threats” against Trump and members of his administration.

Garcia pushed back, saying Congress has the constitutional authority to conduct oversight independently of the White House and will not be deterred by “baseless threats” from the administration or the Justice Department. He argued that voters gave the Democrats a mandate “to root out corruption and abuse.”

The latest exchange comes a week after Garcia issued a blunt warning of his own. On election night, after projections showed Democrats would take control of the House, he addressed the incoming Congress with a two-word message: “Lawyer up.”

Read more

Last week, Garcia also outlined several areas Democrats intend to investigate, including what he described as corruption within the Trump family, corporate misconduct, alleged abuses by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and the administration’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation. He also intends to examine the Trump family’s business dealings, including cryptocurrency and mineral deals, as well as construction projects at the White House.

Commenting on the plans at the time, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said Trump is willing to work with Democrats to deliver results for Americans, but warned that pursuing “sham investigations” and “radical-left policies” would mean acting “against the American people.”

Outgoing Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, a Trump critic, told AP on Wednesday that he hopes the Democrats focus on real issues rather than “stupid things” such as the Russiagate inquiry, an investigation based on debunked claims that Trump’s 2016 campaign colluded with Russia. Massie, who recently lost his primary to a Trump-backed Republican challenger, said he believes there is “real corruption” involving the president and the people around him.

title: Russia’s hockey comeback a ‘return to normality’ – German opposition
content:
The AfD and Left Party have urged respect for a court ruling reinstating Russian national teams despite European boycott threats

Russia’s return to international hockey would mark a “return to normality,” a senior Alternative for Germany (AfD) lawmaker has said, as his party and the Left Party backed Russian participation in the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship despite European boycott threats.  

The statements follow an October 30 ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which overturned Russia’s exclusion from International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) competitions. The German government and hockey federation remain opposed to Russian participation, citing security, political and economic concerns.  

The right-wing AfD and the Left Party have urged Berlin to respect the CAS ruling, which restored Russian national teams’ right to compete internationally.  

“We see this as a return to normality. Of course, Russian athletes should also be issued visas,” Jorn Konig, the AfD parliamentary group’s sports spokesman, told ZDFheute.  

Read more

Russian and Belarusian athletes were barred from numerous international competitions following the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in 2022. Since then, criticism of the bans as politically motivated and discriminatory has grown, with a number of sports federations easing restrictions.  

Konig, who has opposed the Ukraine conflict, accused sporting authorities of double standards, noting that the US had never been excluded from international competitions despite waging wars he described as violations of international law.  

The AfD won September’s regional election in Saxony-Anhalt, defeating Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s CDU.  

Christian Gorke, the Left Party’s sports spokesman, also urged respect for the CAS ruling, saying Germany could no longer ignore the “regrettable reality” of Russia’s return.  

The championship is scheduled for May 13-30, 2027, in Dusseldorf and Mannheim. The IIHF has expressed “disappointment” with the ruling but pledged to comply.  

The German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) opposes Russia’s return, with its chairman, Frank Lutz, warning that the ruling “fundamentally changes the situation,” citing political, economic and security concerns.  

Days earlier, Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Latvia, and the Czech Republic announced boycotts of matches against Russia, while Austria indicated it would follow suit.  

The boycott threats have cast doubt on Germany’s ability to host the tournament. Berlin is consulting hockey officials, warning that the event could become impossible to organize for sporting and economic reasons.  

Read more

Russian officials have condemned the politicization of sport, arguing that athletes should not be punished over geopolitical disputes. Sports Minister and Olympic Committee chief Mikhail Degtyarev branded the threats “infantile” and warned that countries pressuring the IIHF could face legal action or lose hosting rights.  

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov suggested moving the championship elsewhere if Germany refuses to host it, noting that “there are plenty of countries” willing to stage the tournament.  

Earlier this year, the International Olympic Committee provisionally lifted its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee, while several federations have readmitted Russian athletes, sometimes under their national flag and anthem.

title: Durov mocks spy agencies over ‘honeypot’ scandal
content:
The Telegram founder has trolled intelligence agencies for ignoring his dating preferences following an FBI probe into Nvidia boss Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy

Telegram founder Pavel Durov has mocked intelligence agencies for failing to cater to his dating preferences, joking that tech CEOs who aren’t attracted to Asian women are being deprived of “honeypot” opportunities.

In a tongue-in-cheek post on X on Wednesday, the Russian-born billionaire questioned why intelligence services had apparently failed to send female operatives his way who suited his preference for non-Asian women, asking whether they were “even trying.”

He made a pointed exception for France, quipping that its “decision-makers aren’t into girls” – an apparent jab at President Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte, who have sued US podcaster Candace Owens over her claims that France’s first lady was born male. Durov concluded that Paris could be excused, but that everyone else should “try harder” to seduce him.

Unfair that CEOs who aren’t into Asian girls get fewer dating options from spy agencies. Where are the French/Russian/Iranian honeypots? Not one spy girl sent my way. Are they even trying? France is excused — their decision-makers aren’t into girls. Everyone else: try harder!

— Pavel Durov (@durov) November 11, 2026

Not all CEOs are so unlucky

Durov’s remarks follow an espionage scandal involving American AI chipmaking giant Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The controversy erupted in late October after reports linked the CEO to Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese executive formerly associated with Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia chip buyer in Southeast Asia.

US intelligence officials suspect the woman was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to gather information on Nvidia and potentially influence its CEO to push Washington to ease AI chip export restrictions.

Read more

After initially describing their interactions as routine business dealings, Huang admitted last week to an extramarital affair without confirming the name of the woman. Nvidia launched an internal investigation into the alleged honeypot operation.

President Donald Trump confirmed on Monday that the FBI has also opened a probe, but defended Huang, a close ally in Washington’s AI rivalry with Beijing, calling him “an amazing guy” who had been unaware of the alleged espionage.

Beijing has dismissed the allegations as “a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear.” Meanwhile, separate reports have since alleged another affair between Huang and Nvidia healthcare vice president Kimberly Powell, and claimed the company’s board is considering ousting the CEO.

French spies have courted Durov before – just not romantically

While Durov’s apparent disappointment over his lack of suitable “honeypots” was clearly in jest, his relations with French intelligence have been anything but romantic.

Read more

French spies have reportedly targeted the Telegram founder, who holds French citizenship but is based in the UAE, for years. According to the Wall Street Journal, French intelligence teamed up with the UAE back in 2017 to hack his iPhone over concerns about Islamic State militants using Telegram.

In February 2024, French prosecutors opened an investigation into Telegram’s alleged failure to cooperate with law enforcement. The case escalated that August with Durov’s arrest and placement under formal investigation over suspected crimes facilitated through the platform.

Durov denied wrongdoing, calling it “absurd” to hold a platform owner responsible for users’ crimes and accusing Paris of using the case to pressure Telegram into political censorship. He claimed French foreign intelligence pushed him to silence conservative voices ahead of Romania’s 2025 presidential election and censor Moldovan Telegram channels ahead of the country’s 2024 vote, allegedly even offering to influence the judge overseeing his case in exchange for cooperation.

READ MORE: Is Pavel Durov a free-speech champion or an unaccountable tech baron?

France’s foreign intelligence agency, the DGSE, later acknowledged meeting Durov but denied his allegations. The Telegram founder remains under formal investigation. Following more than six hours of questioning in Paris in July, his lawyers said nearly two years of investigations had yielded no evidence against him.
